evidence: mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/auth/SsoService.kt:77 - validateAndLogin() error branch does `val error: SsoError = response.body()` with no runCatching guard; if the server/gateway returns a non-JSON or empty error body (e.g. 502/503 proxy HTML, empty 401), the kotlinx deserialization throws, is swallowed by the outer `catch (e: Exception)` at :82, and `_authState.value = AuthState.Error(e.message)` surfaces a raw 'Expected start of the object' serialization message to the user on the security-critical SSO login path.
mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/auth/SsoService.kt:49 - createMobileToken() error branch has the same unguarded `response.body<SsoError>()`.

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/auth/SsoService.kt:104 - getSession() error branch: same pattern (logout() runs first on 401, but the subsequent bare body() can still throw and mask the real status).

INCONSISTENCY / FIX REFERENCE: the newer methods in the SAME file already harden this exact path - register() (:200), confirmPasswordReset() (:257), updateProfile() (:299) use `runCatching { response.body<SsoError>() }.getOrElse { "...(HTTP ${response.status.value})" }`. The four SSO-core methods should adopt the same guard so a malformed error body degrades to a clean status-based message instead of a raw serialization exception.
